title: Meter-scale quantum interconnects between large quantum processors
authors: Neereja M. Sundaresan, Nicholas Cotaj, Yadav Prasad Kandel, Eric Lewandowski, Christian Robert Longton, Yves Martin, Jae-woong Nah, Kathryn Pooley, Martin Sandberg, Michael Scanlon, Chi Xiong, Emanuil Sashev Yanev, David Abraham, Abhinandan Antony, Vincent Arena, Nicholas Bornman, Khanh Dang, Oliver Dial, Christopher Guarino, Gabriel Haspil, Jared Hertzberg, Kentaro Heya, Swetha Kamlapurkar, Michael Karschner, George Keefe, Eric Liniger, Laura Luo, Thomas G. McConkey, David Olson, Jason Orcutt, Dmitry Ovchinnikov, Timothy Phung, Sankeerth Rajalingam, Michael Selvanayagam, William Shanks, Dongbing Shao, Abigail Shearrow, Adam Stabile, Jiri Stehlik, Joseph Suttle, Jeng-Bang Yau, Eric Zhang
abstract: Modular quantum architecture requires long-distance quantum interconnects to stitch together individual processor modules. Such interconnects, long-distance couplers or L-couplers, must support coherent quantum operation over meter-scale distances and scale to multiple connections between any two modules. Here we demonstrate four L-couplers operating between two 120-qubit IBM Nighthawk R1 superconducting qubit processors. Each L-coupler joins two Nighthawk lattice qubits through two frequency-tunable L-qubits, two RF-SQUID based "i2m" couplers, and 80 cm of superconducting aluminum coax. Each cable installs perpendicular to the processor surface, to enable denser connections, and is joined to the chip by an indium-to-indium room temperature pressure bond made after both modules were mounted. L-coupler modes near 5 GHz, with internal quality factors of 0.86 to 1.09e6, carry relay-based state transfer at a mean network benchmarking fidelity of 99.00%, with a best link of 99.29 +/- 0.07%. We then realize distant CZ gates between lattice qubits in separate modules at a mean fidelity of 94.75%, with a best link of 96.42 +/- 0.28%, and use them to generate entangled states across the two processors, including a demonstration of simultaneous Bell pair generation using two adjacent L-couplers. These four high-fidelity L-couplers establish a practical path to scalable quantum interconnects for modular quantum computing.
summary: This paper reports on the creation and testing of meter-scale quantum interconnects using superconducting qubits. By successfully implementing L-couplers between two large quantum processors, the authors demonstrated high-fidelity quantum state transfer and distant two-qubit gates. This work establishes a critical, practical pathway toward building modular, large-scale quantum computers.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is developing reliable, long-distance quantum interconnects (L-couplers) necessary to scale quantum processors beyond single chip modules.
main_result: The researchers successfully demonstrated high-fidelity state transfer (99.00% mean) and distant CZ gates (94.75% mean) across four meter-scale L-couplers, proving a practical path for modular quantum computing.
method: The experiment involves physically assembling superconducting qubit processors connected by custom L-couplers containing superconducting coax, and then measuring quantum gate fidelities and state transfer efficiencies.
model_or_system: The system uses superconducting qubits (IBM Nighthawk R1) connected via L-couplers, which incorporate frequency-tunable L-qubits and RF-SQUID couplers, spanning superconducting aluminum coax over meter-scale distances.
key_observables: State transfer fidelity, distant CZ gate fidelity, Bell pair fidelity, and GHZ state fidelity.
important_parameters: Meter-scale distances, mean state transfer fidelity of 99.00%, and mean distant CZ fidelity of 94.75%.
main_assumptions: The fidelity measurements are limited by readout error, and the performance relies on the successful physical integration of multiple components (qubits, couplers, and cables).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dual-module assembly with four L-couplers, showing the physical components and the measured performance metrics for state transfer and distant gates.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the need for interconnects, detailing the physical construction of the L-couplers, characterizing the link performance via state transfer and distant gates, and concluding with demonstrations of multi-pair entanglement generation.
why_interesting: This work provides crucial experimental benchmarks for quantum networking, directly addressing the engineering bottleneck of connecting quantum modules, which is highly relevant for theorists modeling scalable quantum architectures.
